title.zh: 卷一百〇一 列傳第三十一: 蕭陶蘇斡 耶律阿息保 蕭乙薛 蕭胡篤
title.en: Volume 101 Biographies 31: Xiao Taosuwo, Yelu Axibao, Xiao Yixue, Xiao Hudu
title.raw: 卷一百〇一 列傳第三十一: 蕭陶蘇斡 耶律阿息保 蕭乙薛 蕭胡篤 Volume 101 Biographies 31: Xiao Taosuwo, Yelu Axibao, Xiao Yixue, Xiao Hudu

sentences.zh: 蕭陶蘇斡耶律阿息保蕭乙薛蕭胡篤

translations.literal: Xiao Taosuwo, Yelu Axibao, Xiao Yixue, Xiao Hudu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Taosuwo, Yelu Axibao, Xiao Yixue, and Xiao Hudu

sentences.zh: 蕭陶蘇斡，字乙辛隱，突呂不部人。

translations.literal: Xiao Taosuwo, courtesy name Yixin'yin, was a man of the Tielubu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Taosuwo, whose courtesy name was Yixin'yin, came from the Tielubu tribe.

sentences.zh: 四世祖因吉，發長五尺，時呼為「長發因吉」。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Yinji had hair five chi long and was called at the time "Long-haired Yinji."
translations.idiomatic: A fourth-generation forebear, Yinji, wore his hair five feet long and was known in his day as "Long-haired Yinji."

sentences.zh: 祖裏拔，奧隗部節度使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Liba was Military Commissioner of the Aowei tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liba served as military commissioner for the Aowei tribe.

sentences.zh: 陶蘇斡謹願，不妄交。

translations.literal: Taosuwo was prudent and cautious and did not associate carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Taosuwo was cautious by nature and would not cultivate casual acquaintances.

sentences.zh: 伯父留哥坐事免官，聞重元亂，挈家赴行在。

translations.literal: His uncle Liuge was dismissed from office on account of an offense; hearing of Chongyuan's rebellion, he took his family to join the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Liuge had been stripped of his post for an offense; when word came of Chongyuan's revolt, he took his household to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 時陶蘇斡雖幼，已如成人，補筆硯小底。

translations.literal: At the time, although Taosuwo was still young, he already behaved like an adult and was appointed a petty clerk for brush and inkstone.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a boy, Taosuwo already comported himself like a grown man and was assigned as a junior clerk in charge of writing materials.

sentences.zh: 累遷祗候郎君，轉樞密院侍御。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Gentleman and then transferred to Palace Attendant in the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Attendant Gentleman and then became a palace attendant in the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 咸雍五年，遷崇德宮使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianyong, he was transferred to Director of the Chongde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xianyong era, he was appointed director of the Chongde Palace.

sentences.zh: 會有訴北南院聽訟不直者，事下，陶蘇斡悉改正之，為耶律阿思所忌。

translations.literal: When someone complained that the North and South Councils had judged cases unjustly, the matter was referred down and Taosuwo corrected them all, for which he was resented by Yelu Asi.
translations.idiomatic: When a petitioner alleged that the North and South Councils had heard cases unfairly, the matter came before Taosuwo, who corrected every ruling—earning the enmity of Yelu Asi.

sentences.zh: 帝欲召用，輒為所沮。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to summon and employ him, but Asi repeatedly obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to bring him into higher office, but each time Yelu Asi blocked it.

sentences.zh: 八年，歷漠北滑水馬群太保，數年不調，嘗曰：「用才未盡，不若閑。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he served as Northern Desert Huashui Horse Herd Grand Guardian; for several years he received no transfer and once said, "When talent is not fully used, it is better to be idle."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was posted as grand guardian of the northern Huashui horse herds beyond the desert; for years he received no promotion, and remarked, "When one's abilities go unused, idleness is preferable."

sentences.zh: 」乾統中，遷漠南馬群太保，以大風傷草，馬多死，鞭之三百，免官。

translations.literal: During Qiantong he was transferred to Southern Desert Horse Herd Grand Guardian; a great wind damaged the grass and many horses died; he was flogged three hundred strokes and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qiantong reign he was made grand guardian of the southern horse herds; when a violent wind ruined the pasture and many horses died, he was given three hundred lashes and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 九年，徙天齊殿宿衛。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was moved to palace guard duty at the Tianqi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was reassigned as a palace guard of the Tianqi Hall.

sentences.zh: 明年，谷價翔踴，宿衛士多不給，陶蘇斡出私廩赒之，召同知南院樞密使事。

translations.literal: The next year grain prices soared; many palace guards could not support themselves, and Taosuwo drew on his private granary to relieve them; he was summoned as Associate Director of Southern Council Privy Council affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year grain prices shot up, and many guards could not make ends meet; Taosuwo opened his private stores to feed them and was thereupon appointed associate director of the Southern Council Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 天慶四年，為漢人行宮副部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqing, he became Deputy Commissioner of the Chinese Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianqing he was named deputy commissioner of the bureau for the Chinese palace.

sentences.zh: 時金兵初起，攻陷寧江州。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin troops had just risen and captured Ningjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin armies had just risen in force and taken Ningjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天祚召群臣議，陶蘇斡曰：「女直國雖小，其人勇而善射。

translations.literal: Tianzuo summoned the ministers for deliberation; Taosuwo said, "Although the Jurchen state is small, its people are brave and skilled at archery."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tianzuo called his ministers into council; Taosuwo said, "Small though the Jurchen realm may be, its warriors are fierce and expert archers.

sentences.zh: 自執我叛人蕭海裏，勢益張。

translations.literal: Since they seized our rebel Xiao Hai'li, their power has grown ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since they took our defector Xiao Hai'li into their ranks, their strength has only swelled.

sentences.zh: 我兵久不練，若遇強敵，稍有不利，諸部離心，不可制矣。

translations.literal: Our troops have long gone untrained; if we meet a strong enemy and suffer even a slight setback, the tribes will lose heart and cannot be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces have long neglected drill; should we meet a formidable foe and suffer the slightest reverse, the tribes will lose heart and slip beyond control.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若大發諸道兵，以威壓之，庶可服也。

translations.literal: For the present plan, nothing is better than raising troops from all circuits in great force to overawe them; then perhaps they may submit.
translations.idiomatic: The sound course now is to muster armies from every commandery at once and overawe them by sheer weight—only then might they yield.

sentences.zh: 」北院樞密使蕭得裏底曰：「如陶蘇斡之謀，徒示弱耳。

translations.literal: Northern Council Privy Commissioner Xiao Delidi said, "A plan like Taosuwo's would only show weakness."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Delidi, privy commissioner of the Northern Council, replied, "A scheme like Taosuwo's would only broadcast our weakness.

sentences.zh: 但發滑水以北兵，足以拒之。

translations.literal: It is enough to deploy troops from north of the Huashui River to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: Troops raised north of the Huashui alone will suffice to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 」遂不用其計。

translations.literal: They therefore did not adopt his plan.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel was rejected.

sentences.zh: 數月間，邊兵屢北，人益不安。

translations.literal: Within several months the frontier troops were repeatedly defeated and the people grew ever more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Within months the border armies were beaten again and again, and popular alarm deepened.

sentences.zh: 饒州渤海結構頭下城以叛，有步騎三萬餘，招之不下。

translations.literal: The Bohai of Raozhou rallied at Goutou's subordinate city in rebellion, with more than thirty thousand foot and horse; summons could not bring them down.
translations.idiomatic: The Bohai people of Raozhou rose at a subordinate city under Goutou, fielding more than thirty thousand infantry and cavalry; no summons could make them submit.

sentences.zh: 陶蘇斡帥兵往討，擒其渠魁，斬首數千級，得所掠物，悉還其主。

translations.literal: Taosuwo led troops to campaign against them, captured their ringleaders, beheaded several thousand, recovered the plundered goods, and returned them all to their owners.
translations.idiomatic: Taosuwo marched against them, seized their leaders, decapitated several thousand rebels, recovered all stolen property, and returned every item to its rightful owner.

sentences.zh: 及耶律章奴叛，陶蘇斡與留守耶律大悲奴為守禦。

translations.literal: When Yelu Zhangnu rebelled, Taosuwo and the garrison commander Yelu Dabeinu held the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yelu Zhangnu rose in revolt, Taosuwo and the capital's garrison commander Yelu Dabeinu organized the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 章奴既平，陶蘇斡請曰：「今邊兵懈弛，若清暑嶺西，則漢人嘯聚，民心益搖。

translations.literal: After Zhangnu was suppressed, Taosuwo petitioned, "Now the frontier troops are slack; if [the emperor] crosses west of the Qinghu Ridge, the Chinese will rally and clamor, and popular morale will shake all the more."
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhangnu was crushed, Taosuwo pleaded, "The border forces are slack; if Your Majesty crosses west of Qinghu Ridge, Han subjects will flock together in defiance and the people's hearts will quail the more.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜罷此行。

translations.literal: Your servant, in his folly, thinks this journey should be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: This humble servant believes the expedition ought to be called off.

sentences.zh: 」不納，乃命陶蘇斡控扼東路，招集散卒。

translations.literal: [The petition] was not accepted; Taosuwo was then ordered to control the eastern route and gather scattered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The counsel went unheeded; instead Taosuwo was ordered to hold the eastern front and rally scattered troops.

sentences.zh: 後以太子太傅致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Later he retired with the title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died in office.

sentences.zh: 耶律阿息保，字特裏典，五院部人。

translations.literal: Yelu Axibao, courtesy name Telidian, was a man of the Five-Yuan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Axibao, whose courtesy name was Telidian, came from the Five-Yuan tribe.

sentences.zh: 祖胡劣，太祖時徙居西北部，世為招討司吏。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hulu, in Taizu's time, moved to the northwest and for generations served as clerks in the pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hulu, in the reign of Taizu, resettled in the northwest, and for generations the family served as clerks in the pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 阿息保慷慨有大志，年十六，以才幹補內史。

translations.literal: Axibao was magnanimous and ambitious; at sixteen he entered service as Inner Scribe on account of his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Axibao was openhanded and ambitious; at sixteen he was appointed Inner Scribe on the strength of his abilities.

sentences.zh: 天慶初，轉樞密院侍御。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqing he was transferred to Privy Council palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianqing era he was transferred to palace attendant in the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 金人起兵，城境上，遣阿息保問之，金人曰：「若歸阿疏，敢不聽命。

translations.literal: When the Jin rose in arms and built fortifications on the border, Axibao was sent to inquire; the Jin said, "If [you] return Ashu, we dare not disobey orders."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin took up arms and fortified the frontier, Axibao was dispatched to inquire; the Jin replied, "If you hand back Ashu, we would not dare refuse your command.

sentences.zh: 」阿息保具以聞。

translations.literal: Axibao reported all of it in full.
translations.idiomatic: Axibao reported the full exchange to the throne.

sentences.zh: 金兵陷寧江州，邊兵屢敗，遣阿息保與耶律章奴等賫書而東，冀以脅降。

translations.literal: When Jin troops took Ningjiang and frontier forces were repeatedly defeated, Axibao was sent with Yelu Zhangnu and others bearing documents eastward, hoping to coerce submission.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin captured Ningjiang and the border armies suffered defeat after defeat, Axibao was sent east with Yelu Zhangnu and others bearing letters, hoping to intimidate the enemy into submission.

sentences.zh: 阿息保曰：「臣前使，依詔開諭，略無所屈。

translations.literal: Axibao said, "On my previous mission I expounded the edict and was in no way bent."
translations.idiomatic: Axibao said, "On my last embassy I delivered the imperial message as instructed and would not yield an inch.

sentences.zh: 將還，謂臣曰：『若所請不遂，無相見。

translations.literal: When I was about to return they told me, 'If our request is not granted, we shall not meet again.'
translations.idiomatic: As I was leaving they told me, 'If our demands are not met, we shall not meet again.'

sentences.zh: 』今臣請獨往。

translations.literal: Now I beg to go alone.
translations.idiomatic: I beg now to go alone.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: [His request] was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 將行，別蕭得裏底曰：「不肖適異國，必無生還，願公善輔國家。

translations.literal: Before departing he took leave of Xiao Delidi, saying, "Your unworthy servant goes to a foreign land and will certainly not return alive; may you well assist the state."
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out he bade farewell to Xiao Delidi, saying, "Your unworthy servant is bound for a foreign land and will surely not return alive; may you govern the realm well in my stead.

sentences.zh: 」既至，阿息保見執。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Axibao was seized.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 久乃遁歸。

translations.literal: After a long time he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long captivity did he escape and make his way home.

sentences.zh: 及天祚敗績，遷都巡捕使。

translations.literal: When Tianzuo suffered a crushing defeat, [Axibao] was made Metropolitan Patrol Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianzuo's crushing defeat, he was appointed metropolitan patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，從阿疏討耶律章奴，加領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Ashu to campaign against Yelu Zhangnu and was additionally appointed General-in-Chief of the Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Ashu against Yelu Zhangnu and was additionally made general-in-chief of the Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 阿疏將兵而東，阿息保送至軍，乃還。

translations.literal: Ashu led his army east; Axibao escorted him to the camp and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ashu marched east with his army; Axibao escorted him to the encampment and then turned back.

sentences.zh: 天祚怒其專，鞭之三百。

translations.literal: Tianzuo was angry at his acting on his own authority and had him flogged three hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo, angered that he had acted on his own authority, had him flogged three hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 尋為奚六部禿裏太尉。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Grand Guardian Tuli of the Six Xi Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed grand guardian tuli of the Six Xi tribes.

sentences.zh: 後阿疏反，阿息保以偏師進擊，臨陣墜馬，被擒。

translations.literal: Later when Ashu rebelled, Axibao advanced with a detached force, fell from his horse in battle, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashu later rebelled, Axibao led a detached column against him, was thrown from his horse in battle, and taken captive.

sentences.zh: 因阿疏有舊得免。

translations.literal: Because of his old ties with Ashu he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to his old friendship with Ashu he was spared.

sentences.zh: 時阿疏頗好殺，阿息保謂曰：「欲舉大事，何以殺為！

translations.literal: At the time Ashu was rather fond of killing; Axibao said to him, "If you wish to accomplish a great undertaking, why make killing your way!"
translations.idiomatic: Ashu was then inclined to slaughter; Axibao told him, "If you mean to accomplish a great undertaking, why make killing your way!"

sentences.zh: 」由是全活者眾。

translations.literal: Because of this many were preserved alive in full.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this counsel a great many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 會阿疏敗，乃還。

translations.literal: When Ashu was defeated, [Axibao] then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashu was defeated, he made his way back.

sentences.zh: 以戰失利，囚中京數歲。

translations.literal: For the battle's failure he was imprisoned at Zhongjing for several years.
translations.idiomatic: For the defeat he was imprisoned at Zhongjing for several years.

sentences.zh: 保大二年，金兵至中京，始出獄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoda, when Jin troops reached Zhongjing, he was first released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoda, when Jin forces reached Zhongjing, he was at last released from prison.

sentences.zh: 尋為敵烈皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Chief of the Dilie Pishi guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made chief of the Dilie pishi guard.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏王淳僭號，屢遣人以書來招。

translations.literal: At this time Prince Chun of Wei had assumed a royal title unlawfully and repeatedly sent men with letters to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Prince Chun of Wei had usurped a royal title and repeatedly sent envoys with letters to win him over.

sentences.zh: 阿息保封書以獻，因諫曰：「東兵甚銳，未可輕敵。

translations.literal: Axibao sealed the letter and presented it, admonishing, "The eastern troops are very sharp; they must not be treated lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Axibao sealed the letter and presented it to the throne, admonishing, "The eastern armies are very sharp; they must not be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 」及石輦鐸之敗，天祚奔竄，召阿息保，不時至，疑有貳心，並怒為淳所招，殺之。

translations.literal: When Shinian Duo was defeated, Tianzuo fled in disarray; he summoned Axibao, who did not arrive in time; suspecting divided loyalty and also angered that Chun had tried to recruit him, [Tianzuo] had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: After Shinian Duo's defeat, as Tianzuo fled in disarray he summoned Axibao, who failed to arrive promptly; suspecting disloyalty and enraged that Chun had tried to recruit him, Tianzuo had him executed.

sentences.zh: 初，阿息保知國將亡，前後諫甚切。

translations.literal: Earlier, Axibao knew the state was about to perish and remonstrated repeatedly with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: From the first, Axibao had seen that the state was doomed and remonstrated again and again with desperate urgency.

sentences.zh: 及死以非罪，人尤惜之。

translations.literal: When he died without crime, people regretted it all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When he was put to death without just cause, the people mourned him all the more.

sentences.zh: 蕭乙薛，字特免，國舅少父房子後。

translations.literal: Xiao Yixue, courtesy name Temian, was descended from the Junior Uncle's younger son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yixue, whose courtesy name was Temian, was a descendant of the junior imperial uncle's younger son.

sentences.zh: 性謹願。

translations.literal: By nature he was prudent and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious and steady by nature.

sentences.zh: 壽隆間，累任劇官。

translations.literal: During Shoulong he repeatedly held weighty offices.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shoulong era he held one weighty post after another.

sentences.zh: 天慶初，知國舅詳穩事，遷殿前副點檢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqing he oversaw Imperial Uncle guard affairs and was promoted Deputy Director of Palace Inspection.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianqing he oversaw imperial-uncle guard affairs and was promoted to deputy director of palace inspection.

sentences.zh: 金兵起，為行軍副都統。

translations.literal: When the Jin armies rose, he became Deputy Commanding General on Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin armies rose, he was made deputy commanding general on campaign.

sentences.zh: 以戰失利，罷職。

translations.literal: For defeat in battle he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After a defeat in battle he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 六年，出為武定軍節度使，遷西京留守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went out as Military Commissioner of Wuding Army and was transferred to Western Capital Garrison Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was posted as military commissioner of the Wuding army and transferred to garrison commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，討劇賊董厖兒，戰易水西，大破之。

translations.literal: The next year he campaigned against the fierce bandit Dong Mang'er, fought west of the Yishui, and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he campaigned against the fierce bandit Dong Mang'er, fought west of the Yishui, and routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 以功為北府宰相，加左僕射，兼東北路都統。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made Chancellor of the Northern Prefecture, with additional title Left Vice Director, and concurrent Commander of the Eastern Route Army.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made chancellor of the Northern Prefecture, with the additional title of left vice director and concurrent commander of the Eastern Route army.

sentences.zh: 十年，金兵陷上京，詔兼上京留守、東北路統軍使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when Jin troops took Shangjing, he was ordered to serve concurrently as Shangjing Garrison Commissioner and Eastern Route Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Jin forces captured Shangjing, he was ordered to serve concurrently as Shangjing garrison commissioner and commander of the Eastern Route army.

sentences.zh: 為政寬猛得宜，民之窮困者，輒加振恤，眾咸愛之。

translations.literal: In governing he balanced lenience and severity; whenever the people were destitute he gave relief, and all loved him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he balanced lenience and severity; whenever the people fell into want he gave relief, and all held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 保大二年，金兵大至，乙薛軍潰，左遷西南面招討使。

translations.literal: In Baoda year two, when Jin armies came in force, Yixue's army collapsed and he was demoted to Southwest Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoda, when Jin armies came in overwhelming force, Yixue's army collapsed and he was demoted to southwest pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以部民流散，不赴。

translations.literal: Because his tribal subjects had scattered, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Because his tribal subjects had scattered, he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 及天祚播遷，給侍從不闕，拜殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: When Tianzuo wandered in exile, [Yixue] supplied attendants without fail and was appointed Director of Palace Inspection.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianzuo wandered in exile, he supplied attendants without fail and was appointed director of palace inspection.

sentences.zh: 凡金兵所過，諸營敗卒復聚上京，遣乙薛為上京留守以安撫之。

translations.literal: Wherever Jin troops passed, defeated soldiers from the camps regathered at Shangjing; Yixue was sent as Shangjing commissioner to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Jin armies passed, defeated soldiers from the camps regathered at Shangjing; Yixue was sent as Shangjing commissioner to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 明年，盧彥倫以城叛，乙薛被執數月，以居官無過，得釋。

translations.literal: The next year Lu Yanlun rebelled with the city; Yixue was held several months and released because he had committed no fault in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Lu Yanlun rebelled with the city; Yixue was held for several months and released because he had committed no fault in office.

sentences.zh: 後為耶律大石所殺。

translations.literal: Later he was killed by Yelu Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later killed by Yelu Dashi.

sentences.zh: 蕭胡篤，字合術隱。

translations.literal: Xiao Hudu, courtesy name Heshu'yin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hudu, whose courtesy name was Heshu'yin.

sentences.zh: 其先撒葛只，太祖時願隸宮分，遂為太和宮分人。

translations.literal: His forebear Sagezhi, in Taizu's time, wished to be enrolled in palace household service and thus became a man of the Taihe palace household.
translations.idiomatic: His forebear Sagezhi, in the reign of Taizu, asked to be enrolled in palace household service and thus became a man of the Taihe palace household.

sentences.zh: 曾祖敵魯，明醫。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dilu was a renowned physician.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dilu was a renowned physician.

sentences.zh: 人有疾，觀其形色即知病所在。

translations.literal: When someone fell ill, by observing complexion and form he knew at once where the disease lay.
translations.idiomatic: When a patient fell ill, he could tell at a glance from complexion and bearing where the affliction lay.

sentences.zh: 統和中，宰相韓德讓貴寵，敵魯希旨，言德讓宜賜國姓，籍橫帳，由是世預太醫選。

translations.literal: In Tonghe, Chancellor Han Derang enjoyed lofty favor; Dilu followed the imperial intent, saying Derang should be granted the imperial surname and enrolled in the horizontal registers, whereupon [the family] for generations entered imperial physician selection.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe era, Chancellor Han Derang enjoyed the highest favor; Dilu read the imperial mood and argued that Derang should be granted the imperial surname and enrolled in the horizontal registers, whereupon the family for generations entered the imperial physician rolls.

sentences.zh: 子孫因之入官者眾。

translations.literal: Many descendants entered office through this connection.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his descendants entered office by this connection.

sentences.zh: 胡篤為人便佞，與物無忤。

translations.literal: Hudu was facile and ingratiating by nature and gave offense to none.
translations.idiomatic: Hudu was smooth and ingratiating by nature and gave offense to no one.

sentences.zh: 清寧初，補近侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning he was appointed to palace attendance.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Qingning he was appointed to palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 大安元年，為彰湣宮太師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an he was made Grand Master of the Zhangmin Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Da'an he was made grand master of the Zhangmin Palace.

sentences.zh: 壽隆二年，轉永興宮太師。

translations.literal: In Shoulong year two he was transferred to Grand Master of the Yongxing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shoulong he was transferred to grand master of the Yongxing Palace.

sentences.zh: 天慶初，累遷至殿前副點檢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqing he was promoted step by step to Deputy Director of Palace Inspection.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianqing he rose step by step to deputy director of palace inspection.

sentences.zh: 五年，從天祚東征，為先鋒都統，臨事猶豫，凡隊伍皆以圍場名號之。

translations.literal: In year five he followed Tianzuo on the eastern campaign as vanguard commanding general; in action he was irresolute; all units were named after hunting parks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Tianzuo on the eastern campaign as vanguard commanding general; in action he was irresolute, and every unit was named after a hunting park.

sentences.zh: 進至剌離水，與金兵戰，敗，大軍亦卻。

translations.literal: Advancing to the Chali River, he fought the Jin and was defeated; the main army also retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to the Chali River, he fought the Jin and was defeated, and the main army fell back as well.

sentences.zh: 及討耶律章奴，以籍私奴為軍，遷知北院樞密使事，卒。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Yelu Zhangnu he mustered private bondsmen as troops; he was transferred to oversight of Northern Council Privy Council affairs and died.
translations.idiomatic: When campaigning against Yelu Zhangnu he mustered his private bondsmen as an army; he was transferred to oversight of Northern Council privy council affairs and died.

sentences.zh: 胡篤長於騎射，見天祚好遊畋，每言從禽之樂，以逢其意。

translations.literal: Hudu excelled at mounted archery; seeing Tianzuo's fondness for hunting, he always spoke of the pleasures of the chase to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Hudu excelled at mounted archery; seeing Tianzuo's love of the hunt, he always spoke of the pleasures of the chase to please him.

sentences.zh: 天祚悅而從之。

translations.literal: Tianzuo was pleased and followed his lead.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo was delighted and followed his lead.

sentences.zh: 國政隳廢，自此始雲。

translations.literal: The ruin of state administration began from this, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The ruin of state administration, it is said, began from this.

sentences.zh: 論曰：甚矣，承平日久，上下狃於故常之可畏也！

translations.literal: Commentary says: How extreme! When peace lasts long, superior and inferior cling to old ways—that is something to fear!
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: How grave a matter! When peace endures too long, those above and below grow attached to the familiar—and that is what should terrify us!

sentences.zh: 天慶之間，女直方熾，惟陶蘇斡明於料敵，善於忠諫，惜乎天祚痼蔽，不見信用。

translations.literal: During Tianqing the Jurchen were flourishing; only Taosuwo was clear in assessing the enemy and skilled in loyal remonstrance—alas, Tianzuo was set in blindness and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqing years the Jurchen were in full ascent; only Taosuwo was clear-eyed in judging the foe and steadfast in loyal remonstrance—yet Tianzuo was set in blindness and would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 阿息保不死阿疏之難，乙薛甘忍盧彥倫之執，大節已失矣，他有所長，亦奚足取。

translations.literal: Axibao did not die in Ashu's peril; Yixue willingly endured Lu Yanlun's seizure; their great integrity was already lost; even if they had other strengths, what is there worth taking?
translations.idiomatic: Axibao did not perish in Ashu's disaster, and Yixue submitted to Lu Yanlun's capture—their paramount integrity was already gone; whatever other talents they possessed, what is there to esteem?

sentences.zh: 胡篤以遊畋逢迎天祚而隳國政，可勝罪哉！

translations.literal: Hudu, by hunting and hawking to court Tianzuo's favor, ruined state administration—can his guilt be fully told!
translations.idiomatic: Hudu ruined the governance of the realm by hunting and hawking to win Tianzuo's favor—what punishment would not be too light!
